findings.title: Blocked email check mutates records during validation
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record every time it is called. It is invoked from EmailValidator while validating User, and UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so a single blocked signup attempt can update the blocked-email row twice. The write also happens even if the user record is ultimately invalid or not saved, and concurrent requests can lose increments because this is a non-atomic read-modify-write. Validation should be read-only; update statistics separately, ideally atomically, if that behavior is desired.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is not normalized, allowing case/whitespace bypass
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email) using the raw value, and neither the model nor the migration normalizes case or whitespace. The changed code also does not downcase or strip the email before validation during account creation. A blocked address such as foo@example.com can therefore be bypassed with Foo@Example.com or surrounding whitespace, and the case-sensitive unique index permits duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. Normalize emails before storing and querying, and use a case-insensitive unique index or normalized column.

findings.title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and under-escaped
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new('@(#{domains})', true) after only escaping dots. The pattern is not anchored to the end of the address, so with a whitelist of example.com, user@example.com.evil.com matches and is treated as allowed. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are also not escaped, which can cause unintended matches or regexp errors. Split the setting into domains, escape each domain, and anchor the match to the actual domain portion of the email address.

findings.title: Rejected emails are stored in a shared/non-reset array
findings.body: rejectedEmails is defined as Em.A([]) on the controller prototype. Mutable array properties on an Ember prototype are shared across controller instances and are not reset when the modal is reopened. Once an email has been rejected, it can remain rejected for the lifetime of the page/controller state even if the form state should be fresh, potentially preventing legitimate retries. Initialize or reset the array per controller instance/modal open.

findings.title: Email validator tests stub the blocked-email check and omit domain-restriction cases
findings.body: The spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and asserts that an error is added or not. It does not exercise the real whitelist/blacklist logic, email normalization, or the side effects of blocked-email matching. Because the domain regex and blocked-email handling are security-relevant, add tests that use real BlockedEmail records and SiteSetting values, including case variations and suffix domains such as user@example.com.evil.com.
